proof:
# Simultaneous localization cannot preserve arbitrary bad-cap inequalities

This note gives an exact obstruction to the proposed localization step:
reduce every continuous fiber law to a law on a line segment, retaining
all integer-fiber mass ratios and every member of a finite collection of
upper bounds on oblique-cap masses. The obstruction holds even if the
line direction and the probability law may be chosen independently in
each fiber. Thus requiring a common direction or exponential needle
density cannot repair that particular statement.

It does not rule out a more selective localization theorem that preserves
a specially chosen subset of constraints, or a decomposition whose
individual needles do not satisfy the constraints. The failed statement
would have required a single simultaneous reduced measure satisfying all
the prescribed bounds.

## Exact source and cap constraints

Let

    T={(x,y):x>=0,y>=0,x+y<=1},
    lambda_0=1-x-y, lambda_1=x, lambda_2=y,
    C=[0,2] x T,
    S=C intersect (Z x R^2)={0,1,2} x T.

The source density is the jointly log-concave function `1_C`. Its
sampled probability measure `mu` gives mass `1/3` to each of the three
fibers and has uniform conditional law on `T`. Each fiber has area
`V=1/2`, so the total unnormalized mass is `3/2`. No fiber has half the
total mass.

For `i=0,1,2` define the closed ambient halfspace

    H_i={(z,x,y):lambda_i(x,y)-z>=1/3}.              (1)

Its normal is nonzero and couples the integer and continuous variables.
For `z=1,2`, (1) misses `T` because `lambda_i<=1`. For `z=0`, it cuts
the simplex cap `lambda_i>=1/3`, whose area is `(2/3)^2 V=2/9`.
Consequently

    mu(H_i)=4/27, i=0,1,2.                         (2)

All three caps are strictly below the sharp OC threshold for `n=1,d=2`,
which is `gamma_2/2=2/9`: the gap is `2/27`. Their union covers the
entire index-zero fiber because `lambda_0+lambda_1+lambda_2=1`.
They do not cover all of `S`, and this construction does not refute OC.

## Impossibility of a simultaneous needle measure

There is no probability measure `nu` supported on `S` that satisfies all
three of the following conditions:

1. Every integer fiber retains mass `1/3`.
2. In each fiber the conditional law is supported on an affine line
   (a point or segment is permitted; no density assumption is needed).
3. `nu(H_i)<=mu(H_i)=4/27` for all three caps in (1).

To prove this, restrict `nu` to the index-zero fiber and normalize it to
a probability law `rho` of total mass one. By condition 2 it is supported
on the compact segment formed by intersecting some line with `T`. A
one-dimensional median point `p` belongs to this segment, and every
closed halfline containing it has conditional mass at least `1/2`:
both closed one-sided intervals through a median have mass at least
`1/2`, and moving the endpoint outwards can only increase that mass.
This includes atomic laws.

At least one `lambda_i(p)>=1/3`. The restriction of the corresponding
`H_i` to the supporting line is a closed halfline containing `p`, or the
whole line. Its conditional mass is at least `1/2`. Therefore

    nu(H_i)>=(1/3)(1/2)=1/6>4/27,

with exact gap `1/54`, contradicting condition 3. Other fibers would
contribute nonnegative mass; here they actually contribute zero because
the measure is supported in `S`. This proves the global obstruction.

The argument uses only the existence of a median on a line. In
particular, allowing arbitrary exponential parameters, different line
directions in different fibers, atoms, endpoint limits, or nonunique
medians does not evade it. Even reducing just the index-zero fiber to a
needle while preserving its mass and the three bounds is impossible.

## A precise simultaneous perturbation space

Here is the natural elementary variation for compactly supported jointly
log-concave densities. Let `f` be such a density on a convex compact set
`C` and let

    h(w)=a dot w+c

be affine. For sufficiently small `|t|`, `1+t h` and `1-t h` are strictly
positive throughout `C`. Both

    f_t^+(w)=f(w)(1+t h(w)),
    f_t^-(w)=f(w)(1-t h(w))

are jointly log-concave: on their positive supports their logarithms are
`log f+log(1+/-t h)`, sums of concave functions. Both vanish outside the
same convex support. Their average is exactly `f`.

Every fiber-mass or cap-mass functional is linear in this variation.
To preserve unnormalized fiber masses one requires

    int f(z,x)h(z,x) dx=0                         (3)

at every retained integer index. To preserve an upper cap bound that is
active at `f` in both signs, one additionally requires

    sum_z int 1_H(z,x)f(z,x)h(z,x) dx=0.           (4)

For normalized ratios one can instead allow the left side of (3) to be
the same scalar times each original fiber mass, and subtract that scalar
from `h`; the constant direction is then irrelevant to the normalized
law. These are an explicit finite system of linear equations on an
ambient affine space of dimension `n+d+1`. Rank, rather than merely the
number of constraints, determines whether a nonzero variation exists.
There is no justification for assuming that its kernel survives when
the number of prescribed fiber and cap constraints grows.

For the exact source above, write

    h(z,x,y)=a z+b x+c y+e.

The three fiber-mass equations (3) give

    a=0, e=-(b+c)/3,                              (5)

because the uniform mean of `x,y` on `T` is `(1/3,1/3)`. The three
equations have rank two. The conditional centroid of the cap
`lambda_1>=1/3` is `(5/9,2/9)`, and that of `lambda_2>=1/3` is
`(2/9,5/9)`. Formula (4) for those two active caps therefore gives

    2b-c=0, -b+2c=0.                              (6)

Their coefficient determinant is three, so `b=c=0`, and (5) then gives
`a=e=0`. Thus the admissible affine perturbation kernel is already zero
at this full-dimensional uniform example. The third cap equation is
consistent but unnecessary for killing the kernel; all three caps are
needed for the simpler global no-needle certificate above.

This establishes both a concrete finite constraint count and a global
obstruction. An attempted induction by localization must change what it
preserves or supply an additional mechanism for disposing of constraints;
it cannot silently apply ordinary two-constraint needle localization
simultaneously to all the fiber ratios and bad caps.

All rational area, centroid, gap, and rank calculations are verified by
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_simultaneous_localization_obstruction.py`.
